To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed an automated pipeline to segment individual astrocytic processes in large scale 3-D multicolor fluorescence microscopy images, that we successfully validated this pipeline against manual annotations and that we applied this pipeline to map the domains occupied astrocytes in mouse cortex during development.
we have designed a pipeline for large scale 3-D color fluorescence microscopy images of astrocytes, and that it has been validated by comparing its performance against other classical methods.
a CNN approach is a powerful tool for segmenting astrocytes in multicolor fluorescence microscopy images.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and evaluating new bioimage analysis methods to support neuroscience research.
the development of novel image processing techniques to analyze and quantify the organization of neural networks in 3D microscopy images.
the development of novel bioimage analysis methods for the study of the brain, which will help to better understand the organization and development at the cellular level of this complex organ.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a new approach for neural cell segmentation that is based on CNN.
the proposed method outperforms classical techniques, and is able to handle the challenging variety of cell shapes, colors, and sizes, and their overlap with other cells and background elements.

the method presented in this paper is able to detect and segment astrocytes in a 3D fluorescence microscopy image with a high accuracy, and it is able to detect the astrocytes even in the presence of other cell types, such as neurons, which have similar shape and size.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully implemented a deep learning approach for the segmentation of individual astrocytes in a large scale 3d multicolor fluorescence microscopy images.
the pipeline we developed is a powerful tool for the analysis of large-scale 3D fluorescence microscopy images of brain tissue.
the proposed method can be applied to a large scale 3d multicolor fluorescence microscopy images and can be applied for neural cell segmentation in developmental neuroscience.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CNNs can be successfully applied in a wide range of problems, even when dealing with complex and large-scale images, such as the one presented in this work.

deep learning techniques can be applied to solve problems that were considered as intractable, and that the resulting algorithms can be used to analyze large amounts of data in order to extract biological information.
deep learning techniques are able to successfully handle the complexity of biological images and to be used for large scale analysis.
